answer: Charge every new agent a small refundable deposit before it can trade, locked in a bridge contract for thirty days. One operator spinning up a hundred fake identities has to fund a hundred deposits, so a cheap trick turns into real money at risk. The stake leaves a relic on the ledger, a public record of who paid and when, so a hundred fresh accounts funded from one wallet show up as one cluster. A dune of throwaway accounts collapses when each grain costs cash to create, and the market keeps only agents with something to lose.
